messages.subject: Re: Group Comparison for 3 sample groups
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

to do this, you run the standard MSstats workflow and while using groupComparison function, you pass a contrast matrix of three comparisons: (1, -1, 0), (1, 0, -1), (0, 1, -1) [or you flip the signs] where first position corresponds to control, second to control2, third to disease.

Kind regards,
Mateusz

messages.subject: Re: Plotting individual replicate FC along with mean point range FC
messages.subject_clean: Plotting individual replicate FC along with mean point range FC
messages.body_plain:
Dear Bhavesh,

I am not sure I fully understand your analysis from the description. But the sentence "split the dataframe by replicates and run msstats dataprocess on individual replicates" doesn't sound like a correct thing to do.

If you are interested in temporal changes, you need to fit the model with all the replicates, and then test the null hypothesis comparing the time points. This can be done by specifying an appropriate contrast.

More generally, hypothesis testing typically focuses on statements regarding the entire populations (i.e., what happens on average over many replicates) as opposed to an individual replicate.

If you had something else in mind, please post your code and (a portion of) an example dataset. Maybe we'll be able to make a more specific comment.

I hope that this helps at least somewhat

Sincerely
OV

messages.subject: Issues with which.proteinid argument in MSstats::PDtoMSstatsFormat
messages.subject_clean: Issues with which.proteinid argument in MSstats::PDtoMSstatsFormat
messages.body_plain:
Hello again,

The default protein identifier in PDtoMSstatsFormat is an accession ID. In order to get more use out of the protein identifier in MSstats (4.2), i started merging the accession ID and the gene symbol to make a unique variable ('gene_accession') that I can understand better. Within the PDtoMSstatsFormat function i change the which.proteinid argument to 'gene_accession', but the output indicates that the function is still using just the accession ID. I'm sure I could just keep using the accession ID, then left_join a data frame with the gene symbols and other useful protein annotation columns but I wanted to make sure I wasn't horribly messing something up. I've attached a sample of the feature data (sample_df), annotation data, and the log output file from the PDtoMSstatsFormat function.

I appreciate the help,
Best,
Scott
